X = [ 0  1 ]    Y = [ 0  -i ]    Z = [ 1   0 ]
    [ 1  0 ]        [ i   0 ]        [ 0  -1 ]

All three: Hermitian, unitary, G^2 = I
caption: No adjustable parameter, and each gate undoes itself if applied twice.

steps.label: X|0⟩ = |1⟩, X|1⟩ = |0⟩
steps.sub: The "quantum NOT" — it just swaps the two amplitudes

steps.label: Y|0⟩ = i|1⟩, Y|1⟩ = -i|0⟩
steps.sub: Same bit flip as X, plus a ±i phase factor on the result

steps.label: |i|² = |-i|² = 1
steps.sub: Measurement probabilities are unaffected by that phase

steps.label: That phase is not nothing
steps.sub: It's exactly the ingredient interference-based algorithms use later

steps.label: Z|0⟩ = |0⟩, Z|1⟩ = -|1⟩
steps.sub: No bit flip at all — only a sign appears on the |1⟩ amplitude

steps.label: Measurement probabilities: [0.5, 0.5] before AND after
steps.sub: A sign disappears the moment you square the amplitude

steps.label: Relative phase is invisible to a lone measurement
steps.sub: ...but it becomes observable once combined with an interfering gate

subtitle: The gate that turns a definite state into genuine superposition.
